subject: operating-systems
title: Working sets and page replacement
summary: A working set approximates the pages actively used in a recent window and helps reason about locality and thrashing.

questions.prompt: What does the working-set window represent?
options: A recent interval of memory references used to estimate active pages
The number of files in a directory
questions.answerKey: The window is a recent reference interval from which the distinct active pages are estimated.
questions.explanation: The window can be defined by time or reference count.

options: Excessive paging that leaves little time for useful execution
questions.answerKey: Thrashing occurs when page faults and replacement dominate useful computation.
questions.explanation: It often indicates insufficient frames for the workload’s locality.

questions.prompt: Reference string 1,2,1,3 with a window of the last three references has which working set at the end?
questions.answerKey: The last three references are 2,1,3, so the distinct pages are {1,2,3}.
questions.explanation: The set counts distinct pages, not repeated references.

questions.prompt: Why can increasing the working-set window increase estimated memory demand?
options: A longer window can include more distinct pages from different phases
It reduces the number of references to zero
It forces every page to be executable
questions.answerKey: A longer history may span more locality phases and therefore include more distinct pages.
questions.explanation: The estimate depends on the reference pattern.

questions.prompt: For references 1,2,3,2,4 and a window of 4 ending at the last reference, compute the working set.
questions.answerKey: The last four references are 2,3,2,4, so the working set is {2,3,4}, with three distinct pages.
questions.explanation: A working set is a set of pages, not a sequence with repeated entries.

questions.prompt: A process repeatedly alternates between two phases, each using four pages, but only three frames are allocated. Explain why faults may be high and suggest a response.
questions.answerKey: Three frames cannot hold either four-page phase, so references can evict pages that the phase immediately needs, causing repeated faults. Allocate enough frames for the active working set if possible, reduce competing load, or use a policy that detects thrashing and suspends/rebalances processes.
